text: Two girls clap their hands together. What are the girls doing?
The girls are clapping their hands.
The first sentence is about two girls. Change it to talk about only Mia.
Mia is clapping her hands.
Two girls face each other. Find and fix one word in the sentence.
The girls are facing each other.
Two girls play a game together. What are the girls doing?
The girls are playing a game.
Mia claps her hands. What is Mia doing?
Mia is clapping her hands.
Mia faces Jo, and Jo faces Mia. Which way are the girls facing?
The girls are facing each other.
You mop the floor to help the teacher. How do you help?
I help by mopping the floor.
You say, I clean the floor. Change this into a sentence that tells how you help.
I help by cleaning the floor.
You and Jo give books to children to help the teacher. Fix one word in the sentence.
We help by giving books to children.
You give books to children to help the teacher. How do you help?
I help by giving books to children.
You and Jo clean the floor to help the teacher. How do you and Jo help?
We help by cleaning the floor.
You mop the floor to help the teacher. How do you help?
I help by mopping the floor.
In this story, two parents cook food. They wash clothes too. Tell me both actions in one sentence.
They cook food and wash clothes.
These story parents take Leo to school. They wash clothes too. Join the two sentences and say they only once.
They take Leo to school and wash clothes.
The story parents do both jobs every day: cooking food, checking homework. Fix the word that joins the jobs.
They cook food and check homework.
These story parents cook food. They check homework too. Tell me both actions in one sentence.
They cook food and check homework.
These story parents take Leo to school. They wash clothes too. Tell me both actions in one sentence.
They take Leo to school and wash clothes.
These story parents wash clothes. They cook food too. Tell me both actions in one sentence.
They wash clothes and cook food.
At school, Mia says please and thank you. Which word describes her kind words? Use a full sentence.
Mia is polite at school.
Before, Mia used a kind word. Now she waits calmly for her turn. Which word describes her waiting? Use a full sentence.
Mia is patient.
Tom says please and thank you. Fix the word that describes his kind words.
Tom is polite.
Mia says please and thank you. Which word describes her kind words? Use a full sentence.
Mia is polite.
Tom waits calmly for his turn. Which word describes his waiting? Use a full sentence.
Tom is patient.
Jo waits calmly for the bus. Which word describes her waiting? Use a full sentence.
Jo is patient.
Children need help finding books in the library. Who helps them? Say who it is and what the person does.
A librarian helps children find books.
Before, we needed a helper at the pool. Now people need to cross the street. Who helps them? Say who it is and what the person does.
A crossing guard helps people cross the street.
This person leads the school. Find and fix the job name.
The principal leads the school.
Children need help finding books at the library. Say who helps and what the person does.
A librarian helps children find books.
People need help in the water at a pool. Say who helps and where the person helps.
A lifeguard helps people at the pool.
Who leads the school? Use a full sentence.
The principal leads the school.
In this classroom, cleaning up is okay. What can we do? Use a full sentence.
We can clean up the classroom.
The old rule says games are okay. The new rule says no games now. Change the sentence.
We cannot play now.
The classroom rule says no fighting. Find and fix one word in the sentence.
We cannot fight in the classroom.
This classroom rule says cleaning up is okay. What can we do? Use a full sentence.
We can clean up the classroom.

We cannot fight in the classroom.
This classroom rule says helping the teacher is okay. What can we do? Use a full sentence.
We can help the teacher.
